sn32.1:1.2: _Valāhaka_ is not explained in any dictionary I have seen, and I have not been able to trace it in pre-Buddhist texts. I posit a basic meaning of _vala_ as “horse”, hence _vāla_ (“horse-hair”). Appended with _āha_ (“sky”) we have _valāhaka_ the “sky-horse”, which is the name of the horse of the universal monarch ([mn129:37.2]()), and metaphorically the “clouds”. The link between horses and clouds recalls the Vedic Maruts, boisterous gods of the thunderclouds, who roamed about roaring in their chariot drawn by horses (Rig Veda 1.39.6, 1.87.4, 1.88.1, 5.42.15, etc.), which (RV 5.53.7. Pegasus, who was said by Hesiod to be the the bringer of thunderbolts to Zeus, may stem from the same mytheme.
